NEW src/engine/adr-scaffold.ts. root discovery, max+1 allocation, §4.1 template rendering, `project.architecture.decisions` honoured with a `docs/decisions` default (FR-002, FR-003, FR-019). Tests: src/engine/adr-scaffold.test.ts

REVIEW FAIL (uat): US-001 concurrent allocation — Expected: two concurrent `gwrk define adr` runs compute the same number and the second fails loudly with `ADR-NNN already exists: docs/decisions/<path>` and exit 1 (FR-002, TC-015). Actual: reproduced 5/5 against a corpus of ADR-001 — both runs exited 0 and wrote `ADR-002-alpha-one.md` and `ADR-002-beta-two.md`, the silent-sibling flaw FR-002 names as the second flaw of the research allocator. See spec.md > US-001, FR-002 Error States, TC-015. Root cause: in `scaffold()` (src/engine/adr-scaffold.ts) both processes complete the `readRecordEntries` re-read before either writes, so the check sees no conflict, and the `wx` flag only refuses an identical filename — a different slug at the same number passes. Fix: make the number claim atomic rather than check-then-write. Create the record with `flag: "wx"` at the allocated number FIRST, then on `EEXIST` re-read and retry the allocation (or fail naming the conflicting path); alternatively scan for any `ADR-NNN-*.md` immediately after the write and refuse if a second one is present. Add a non-mocked regression to src/engine/adr-scaffold.test.ts that drives two overlapping `scaffold()` calls against a real temp directory and asserts exactly one record exists at the number and the loser rejects — the existing mocked-fs test forces a state the real filesystem sequence never produces, which is why this shipped green.
